solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: By Eurythmics originally, inferior song's covered

indicators.note: the record's lesser side is wrapped around the band's first letter, covering it

parts.note: the B-side of a single was the lesser track, so an inferior song is a B-SIDE

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the band's name

explanation.surface: A pop-music snippet: an early Eurythmics track relegated to the flip side of a single.
explanation.walkthrough: The record's flip side is written BSIDE without its hyphen; the E from Eurythmics goes after its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are prepositions of position: standing by a thing is standing next to it.

clue.text: Turn white left in place where you'd usually do the opposite

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is placed inside the seaside spot

parts.words: place where you'd usually do the opposite
parts.note: people lie on a beach to get a tan, the opposite of going pale

explanation.surface: A wry observation about going pale at the seaside where everyone else browns.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of turning white is getting a tan, which is what people go to the beach for.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove colour with chemicals or sunlight is a verb meaning to make or go pale.

clue.text: Cricket shot from Boycott after cluster of wickets

indicators.note: the word for boycott comes after the word for the cluster of wickets

parts.note: in cricket the square is the central part of the ground where the pitches (wickets) are laid side by side
to boycott something is to cut it, refuse to deal with it

explanation.surface: Cricket commentary: Geoffrey Boycott playing a stroke after a clatter of wickets fell.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous Yorkshire and England opening batsman, so the capital B leads you to cricket rather than to a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A batting stroke played horizontally, hitting the ball away on the off side at right angles to the pitch.

clue.text: Envoy's reduced qualification

indicators.note: the word for envoy is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A diplomat whose credentials have been downgraded.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate awarded on completing a course of study is an academic credential.

clue.text: Talked about the woman's teeth

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for talked is read backwards

parts.note: a criminal who talked to the police sang
something belonging to the woman is hers

explanation.surface: Gossip about a woman's teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talked about' sounds like a sound-alike signal, but 'about' reverses SANG (talked, as an informer does) to give GNAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang British word for teeth, especially false ones, from the verb for grinding them.

clue.text: With pound to put in, need coin OK to work jukebox

indicators.note: the abbreviation for pound has to be inserted into the rearranged letters
the letters of the phrase are worked into a new order

parts.note: L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Instructions for feeding a jukebox: put in your pound, you need a coin to make it play.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffling NEED COIN OK gives NICKEODEON; L goes in after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage this was an early coin-operated music machine, a name later used for jukeboxes.

clue.text: Ancient battle for sausages

definitions.meaning: the sea battle of 480 BC where the Greek fleet beat the Persians

explanation.surface: An odd pairing of classical warfare and deli fare.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves both the Greek island where the Persian fleet was defeated and the Italian cured meats.

clue.text: Girl climbing tree by yard

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the tree is reversed

parts.note: a lime (linden) is a tree

explanation.surface: A girl shinning up a tree in the back yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Small strip as summer clothing

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A skimpy little strip of fabric passed off as summer wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, sleeveless frock worn in hot weather is a warm-season garment.

clue.text: Provides with jokes from the internet?

parts.note: the prefix e- marks something electronic or online, as in email
quips are witty jokes

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps you supplied with funny material found online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provides with' is the definition: you equip someone with tools.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with what they need is to supply them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Rough servant one charged after row

indicators.note: the charged particle comes after the rowing word

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A servant who was blamed for a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests an accusation and 'row' a quarrel; they are a charged particle and rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen drudge doing the lowliest menial jobs, an old term for a base or low servant.

clue.text: Decorative feature of vehicle I've hit!

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a fencer calls touché to acknowledge a hit

explanation.surface: A driver shouting after crashing into an ornamental feature.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental scroll-shaped tablet or oval frame, as round royal names in Egyptian hieroglyphs.

clue.text: Pirate not well armed

parts.note: the Peter Pan villain lost a hand to the crocodile and wears a hook in its place, so he is short of an arm in a sense

explanation.surface: A pirate who is poorly equipped with weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armed' means carrying weapons on the surface, but the joke is a missing hand on one arm.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's buccaneer had one hand replaced by an iron hook, so one arm is incomplete.

clue.text: Official dressing king

parts.note: mayo, short for mayonnaise, is a salad dressing
R (Rex) is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A courtier helping the king to get dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests putting on clothes; it is salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The elected head of a town council is a civic dignitary, a kind of public officer.

clue.text: Posh mini crashed in men's competition

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for men

parts.note: chaps are men; the possessive merely joins the surface

indicators.note: the little car crashed, so its letters with posh's are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A smart little car crashing during a men's motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashed' scrambles POSH MINI, and 'men's' only looks possessive: it gives the plain word for men, which wraps that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest or series of contests to decide the title-holder is a tournament.

clue.text: Camping on island on purpose

parts.note: someone camping is in a tent
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone camping on an island deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On purpose' reads as one phrase, but the second 'on' gives its own letters and 'purpose' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or plan someone means to carry out is their goal, a synonym.

clue.text: Son in fashion house upset wine — chaos

indicators.note: the abbreviation for son goes inside the fashion house's name

parts.note: Dior is a Paris fashion house

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the wine is read upwards

parts.note: red is wine

explanation.surface: A son spills wine at a fashion house and causes mayhem.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of confusion and lack of order is mayhem, a synonym.

clue.text: Avant-garde Bohemian taste facing common problem

indicators.note: something avant-garde is experimental and radically rearranged, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Artists sharing an unconventional, bohemian taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avant-garde' looks like a description of the taste; it is the anagram signal for BOHEMIAN TASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sharing a predicament with others, all facing the same trouble together.

clue.text: Choose artist, complex character

parts.note: to elect is to choose
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Picking a painter with a complicated personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' is the psychological term: Jung named a complex after this mythical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek tragic heroine who avenged her father gave her name to a psychoanalytic complex.

clue.text: Head presents alumnus with some poetry

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A headteacher presenting a former pupil with a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher; it is the heads side of a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The side of a coin bearing the monarch's portrait is the heads face, the opposite of the reverse.

clue.text: Going up a trail

parts.note: a scent is the trail left for hounds to follow

explanation.surface: A walker heading uphill along a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb or rise is the act of moving upwards, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Colour coach-horse regularly displayed

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here starting from the second

explanation.surface: A coach-horse whose coat colour shows evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish-brown earth pigment, and the shade named after it.

clue.text: One brave knight, one in siege

parts.note: a hero is one who is brave
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A brave knight defending a besieged castle.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'siege' is the collective noun for a group of these birds, not a military blockade.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird; a gathering of them is called a siege.

clue.text: Disappointing spectacles opening in Roman days

indicators.note: the opening is put inside the Roman calendar days

parts.note: the nones were days in the ancient Roman calendar, the ninth day before the ides
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: Disappointing shows at the start of the Roman games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman days' suggests a plural like days of the week; the Nones were fixed dates in the Roman month, used in the calendar alongside the Ides.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasions that were hyped but turn out to be anticlimaxes are letdown spectacles.

clue.text: Dull colour's kept in proportion the last time?

indicators.note: the proportion is kept in the colour word, surrounded by it

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
a ratio is a proportion

explanation.surface: A painter's query about how a dull colour was kept in proportion last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last time' is a playful definition: the time something lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The length of time something continues, the time over which it lasts, read cryptically from the phrase.

clue.text: Stew makes British grow

parts.note: to raise crops is to grow them

explanation.surface: A recipe for British home-grown stew.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook slowly in a little liquid in a closed pot is to simmer, a cooking synonym.

clue.text: Rifles National Security Agency kept in shelves

indicators.note: the agency's initials are kept inside the shelving word

parts.note: racks are shelves
NSA is the abbreviation for the US National Security Agency

explanation.surface: Spies keeping their guns stored on shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifles' looks like a noun for guns; it is the verb, to search through.
explanation.definitionFit: To search a place thoroughly and plunder it is to loot, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Seed Greek character planted in compost material

indicators.note: the letter is planted inside the compost word

parts.note: peat is used in compost
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A gardening tip about sowing a seed in compost.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut is botanically a legume seed, the edible kernel inside the pod.
